quote: If we want things to stay as they are, things will have to change.
source: Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa, The Leopard, chapter 1 (Tancredi Falconeri) (trans. Archibald Colquhoun, 1960)
speaker: Tancredi Falconeri
note: The locator is corrected. Colquhoun's English text is divided into chapters, not parts, and Tancredi says this in chapter 1, Introduction to the Prince. The page and imprint proposed, Harvill 1996 p. 19, could not be confirmed: printings differ, one giving p. 19 and another p. 29, so the page is dropped.

evidence.where: two independent citations of Colquhoun's wording and the novel's chapter structure, the book itself being in copyright and not openly readable
evidence.edition: The Leopard, trans. Archibald Colquhoun (1960); wording cited from the Fontana 1963 and Vintage printings
evidence.locator: chapter 1, Introduction to the Prince, Tancredi to his uncle Don Fabrizio

reason: Colquhoun's sentence is quoted identically in both sources, in its full context: 'Unless we ourselves take a hand now, they'll foist a republic on us. If we want things to stay as they are, things will have to change.' The speaker is Tancredi Falconeri and the chapter is the first. Only the part numbering and the unconfirmed page needed changing.
